description: Catalogs and icons, as a store reads them. A 'catalog' case gives the catalog's file 'name' (its extension selects the format), its 'text', and 'base', the source the catalog file came from, against which relative sources resolve; 'expect' gives the 'form' ('minimal' when every entry is a string), the catalog's own informational fields, the 'entries' it lists (each 'source' parsed and made absolute, with 'pin', 'description' and 'about' when present and valid), the entries it 'refused' ([name, class], by name), and the informational fields it 'ignored' (pointers, sorted); or the error that refuses the whole catalog. A 'catalogs' case gives several catalogs, each with the 'label' the consumer gave it, and names to 'choose'; 'expect' gives the listing by identity and label ('shown' is qualified '<label>/<name>' when more than one catalog offers the identity), the 'collisions', and what each requested name picks ('catalog' and 'name', or 'ambiguous' or 'not-found'); or 'invalid-label'. An 'icon' case gives a file 'name', its bytes as 'base64' and optional 'limits'; 'expect' gives the format and dimensions, or the class of the refusal.

catalog.name: catalog.toml
catalog.text:
# A catalog in the full form: the registry format, with informational fields a store lists and
# searches before it fetches anything. registry.json, registry.toml and registry.yaml are catalogs
# in the minimal form. Relative sources and icons resolve beside this file. Its skills table is what
# an overlay's bare skill names resolve through.
name = "Example overlays"
description = "The overlays of the AOS examples, listed for a store."
homepage = "https://example.org/overlays"

# A string entry is the minimal form, a table the full form; one catalog may mix them.
[overlays.engineering]
source = "../engineering"
description = "Shared engineering practices and review guidance."

[overlays.engineering.about]
summary = "Repository-wide engineering practices."
icon = "icons/engineering.png"
tags = ["engineering", "review"]

[overlays.python-review]
source = "../dependent"

[overlays.python-review.about]
summary = "Python review guidance, on top of engineering."
icon = "icons/python-review.png"
license = "MIT"
tags = ["python", "review"]

[overlays.release-notes]
source = "../about"
pin = "sha256:8280aaf5de7c4f61342f648586d534e481ae095cef223dded70f5b1db5bd84a1"

[overlays.release-notes.about]
summary = "Release notes and changelogs, written the same way in every repository."
icon = "icons/release-notes.png"
homepage = "https://example.org/overlays/release-notes"
repository = "https://github.com/example/overlays"
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
authors = ["Example Docs Team <docs@example.org>"]
tags = ["documentation", "release", "changelog"]

# A skill's entry has the fields of an overlay's. Skills and overlays are listed apart: one name can
# be both.
[skills.pdf]
source = "https://github.com/example/skills.git#skills/pdf"
ref = "v1.2.0"
description = "Reads and fills PDF files."

cases.description: A document that is the mapping itself, with no overlays table, is not a catalog.
overlays is a table.
A catalog has an overlays table or a skills table.
A catalog at a URL cannot name a file: URL, Git or not.
A catalog on this machine may name a file: URL.
A catalog from elsewhere: a credential or query, a host that is this machine, a scheme before a path, and a location that is not Git or the web are refused; a private address is not.
A catalog on this machine is the user's own: credentials and other schemes stay, to be shown without them.
A catalog of skills alone, as strings, resolved beside the catalog.
Overlays and skills in one catalog keep apart: a name may be both.
A table entry makes the catalog full; a skill's entry takes the fields an overlay's does.

catalog.name: catalog.toml
catalog.text:
[overlays]
review = "../review"

[skills.pdf]
source = "https://github.com/example/skills.git#skills/pdf"
ref = "v1"
pin = "sha256:abababababababababababababababababababababababababababababababab"
description = "Reads PDF files."

cases.description: Skills resolve like overlays: a relative source in a Git catalog is the same repository, and a local source is refused.
Skill entries are refused alone: names by the skill name rule, equal without ASCII case, and fields as for an overlay.
skills beside overlays and not a table is reported; the overlays are still listed.
overlays beside skills and not a table is reported; the skills are still listed.
Neither table: not a catalog.
A catalog that cannot be read is refused whole.
A name two catalogs offer is shown once per catalog, qualified by its label, never merged; an unqualified request for it is ambiguous. A refused entry collides with nothing.
Two catalogs listing the same source are still two entries.
Names no other catalog offers are shown as written.
Labels are the consumer's, unique when normalized.
A label is a valid overlay name.
A PNG: its format and dimensions.
A lossless WebP (VP8L): width and height are read apart.
A lossy WebP (VP8).
A WebP with an extended header (VP8X): the canvas size.
The extension ignores ASCII case.
SVG is not an icon format, whatever it holds.
Content that is no PNG or WebP is refused, whatever its name says.
A name without an extension names no format.
The content must be the format its extension names.
And the other way round.
Over the consumer's size limit.
Over the consumer's width limit.
Over the consumer's height limit.
A header claiming 4096 x 4096 is refused from the header, before decoding.
Exactly at the limits is accepted.
A PNG signature with no header.
A dimension of zero.
A RIFF size past the end of the file.
A WebP whose first chunk is none of VP8, VP8L and VP8X.
